pamphlet_excerpts: Carving Modeling Tools: Carving and modeling tools come in an amazing array, and most are made of wood, metal, or plastic.
Discarded Sterilized Steel: Discarded (and sterilized) steel dental tools are excellent for detailing, as are wood-carving tools.
Restaurant Suppliers: Restaurant suppliers and hardwareand kitchenware stores are great sources for tools that canbe used in pottery making.
Experienced Potter Probably: An experienced potter probably has collected a variety oftools, but beginners will do well with a basic tool set from aclay supplier.
step_by_step_procedure: Sets Commonly Contain: These sets commonly contain a sponge, a metalrib, a rubber rib, a metal loop tool, a wooden stick, a metalneedle tool, a fettling knife.
Pottery Toolsshould Kept: Pottery toolsshould be kept handy and safe in a sturdy container.
Instance Small Smooth: For instance, small, very smooth riverstones are usefulfor burnishingand compressingclay surfaces, as are spoons.
Seashellsor Pineconesto: Use seashellsor pineconesto make interesting textureson pottery.

pamphlet_excerpts: Stoneware Fires Higher: Stoneware fires to higher temperatures, which leaves the surfacevery hard and nonporous.
Opaque But Thinlypotted: It is usually opaque, but when thinlypotted can be somewhat translucent.
Stoneware Plasticthan: Stoneware is more plasticthan porcelain, which makes it much easier to use in throwingon the wheel or in hand-building.
Natural Clays Stoneware: Some natural clays are stoneware, but often several clays are combined to make a stonewareclay body.
step_by_step_procedure: Kinds Porcelain Objects: Some kinds of porcelain objects are known aswhiteware, including some restaurant and hotel china, finechina, and plumbing fixtures.
Chinais Kind Porcelain: Chinais a kind of porcelain that has special properties.
Usuallyfired High Maturing: It is usuallyfired to a high maturing temperature before being glazed at alower temperature.
Ingredients Recipesare Type: The ingredients in the recipesare what give each type of pottery its distinguishing qualities.

pamphlet_excerpts: Cone Packs Clearly: Make sure cone packs are clearly visible through thepeepholes in the door or sides of the kiln.
Not Themtoo Close: Do not place themtoo close to the peephole or it might be hard to tell which coneis which.
Placed Too Far: If placed too far away among other vague outlines, itmight be difficult to tell what is a cone and what is not.
Conesare Easily Seen: Conesare most easily seen against a plain, solid background, whetherin front of a large pot or with nothing just behind them.
step_by_step_procedure: Extremely Ensure Smallchild: It is extremely important to ensure that no one, a smallchild or a pet, for instance, will interfere with the kiln in anyway during this.
There Special Process: There is a special process for measuring kiln temperature.
Regular Thermometer: No regular thermometer could withstand the extreme heat in a kiln, but many types of firing require the potter to know theactual temperature.
Pyrometer High-temperaturethermometer: A pyrometer, a high-temperaturethermometer, is used for this.

pamphlet_excerpts: Archaeologists Czech: Archaeologists in the Czech Republic have uncovered humanmade ceramics that they believedate to at least 24,000 B.C.
Theseartifacts Form Slabs: Theseartifacts are in the form of slabs, balls, and animal- and human-shapedfigures, and are made of animal fat, bone, bone ash, and a claylike.
Earliest Clay Vessels: The earliest clay vessels were sun-dried, not fired.
Theyprobably Store Grain: Theyprobably were used to store only grain and other dry foods, because filling them with water would have caused the clay toabsorb the liquid.
step_by_step_procedure: Not Long Crude: Not long after these first crude Neolithic meansclay vessels were made, people learned how to use fire to make “new stone” them stronger, harder.
Pottery Jomon Means: This pottery is called Jomon, which means “cord markings,” because much of it was decoratedwith cord patterns.
Pot Shards Foundin: Pot shards foundin other Japanese sites are believed tobe even older, by about 500 years.
Add Details Eyes: Step 4, Add details, such as eyes, hair, fur, whiskers, etc., using a toothpick, needle tool, paper clip, or other sharp tool.

pamphlet_excerpts: Ceramics Industry Largest: The ceramics industry is one of the largest industries in the United States.
Ceramics Useful Their: Ceramics are useful because of their chemical, electrical, mechanical, thermal, magnetic, and structuralproperties.
Ceramics Industry Vital: The ceramics industry is vital to the successfuloperation of other industries.
Abrasive Materials Madefrom: Abrasive materials madefrom silica are essential to the machine-tool and automotiveindustry.
step_by_step_procedure: Glass Products Essential: Glass products are essential to the automobile industryand to architectural, electronic, medical, and agricultural industries.
Uranium Oxide Fuels: Uranium oxide fuels are packaged in ceramic rods for useby nuclear power plants.
Chips Computer Areceramic: The chips in every computer areceramic, as are the tiles that covered NASA’s space shuttles.
Coatingon Paper Formagazines: Even the coatingon paper used formagazines andbooks is ceramic.

requirements.req_text: With your parent or guardian's permission and your counselor's approval, do ONE of the following: (a) Visit the kiln yard at a local college or other craft school. Learn how the different kinds of kilns work, including low fire electric, gas or propane high fire, wood or salt/soda, and raku. (b) Visit a museum, art exhibit, art gallery, artists' co-op, or artist's studio that features pottery. After your visit, share with your counselor what you have learned. (c) Using resources from the library, magazines, the internet (with your parent or guardian's permission), and other outlets, learn about the historical and cultural importance of pottery. Share what you discovered with your counselor.

pamphlet_excerpts: High-fire Kilns Built: Because many high-fire kilns are built by individuals, eachkiln follows a unique schedule.
Not Attempt Fire: Do not attempt to fire anyfuel-burning kiln without close supervision from the owner.
Copper Oxide Canproduce: Copper oxide canproduce a brilliantred in a reductionfiring, but it wouldproduce greens inan oxidation firing.
Fuel Sufficient Amount: Fuel must have a sufficient amount of oxygen to burn.
step_by_step_procedure: Thedampers Fuel-burning: Thedampers in fuel-burning kilns enable the potter to adjust theamount of oxygen inside the kiln.
Kiln Contains Morethan: When the kiln contains morethan enough oxygen needed to completely burn the amount offuel being used, the atmosphere inside the kiln is oxidized.
Reduction Firing Flame: In a reduction firing, the flame is seeking oxygen inside thekiln, and because there isn’t enough, it “steals” oxygen fromthe clay and glazes.
Chemical Reaction Darkens: This chemical reaction darkens the clayand changes the look and texture of some glazes.

pamphlet_excerpts: Collegeeducation Veryhelpful: A collegeeducation is veryhelpful to gain a thoroughunderstanding of the technicalaspects of thisrapidly expandingindustry.
Manyuniversities Andcolleges: Manyuniversities andcolleges offercourses inceramics, the The field of ceramics is extremely diverse, offering manypossibilities for employment.
Interest Thetechnical Fields: You might have an interest in thetechnical fields, chemical, mechanical, or ceramic engineering.
Maybe Prefer Executive: Or maybe you prefer the executive side, such as managingceramic manufacturing operations.
step_by_step_procedure: Special Attention Art: Give special attention to art because it is closelyallied with ceramic design and decoration.
Knowledge Ofmachinery: Also, a knowledge ofmachinery and drafting would be of great help.
Studying Ceramics School: If you are studying ceramics in school, some practicalexperience under actual working conditions would be of value.
Locate Pottery Studio: Try to locate a pottery studio in your community, then apply forpart-time or summer work there.
